cards.back: **Wired** (Ethernet, RS-485, CAN, PLC): high throughput, **deterministic** timing, reliability, security → industrial/fixed. **Wireless** (WiFi, BLE, Zigbee, LoRa, cellular): flexibility, mobility, cheap deployment, scale → consumer/mobile.

Bandwidth, latency, range, power, scalability, reliability, security, cost, topology flexibility, interoperability. Plus **constrained devices / constrained-node networks** (limited CPU/memory/power).

cards.front: Ethernet standard + OSI layers + why for IoT?
cards.back: **IEEE 802.3**, defines **physical + data-link** layers, star topology, MAC addressing. For IoT: **reliability, determinism, PoE, security**.
**MAC** = unique **hardware** ID for local delivery (**Layer 2**). **IP** = **logical** address for routing across networks/internet (**Layer 3**).

cards.front: Switch vs router in an IoT LAN?
cards.back: **Switch** = Layer 2, forwards frames by **MAC** within the LAN (no flooding). **Router** = Layer 3, does **NAT** (private↔public IP), gateway to the **WAN/internet**.

cards.front: What is PoE and its roles?
cards.back: **Power over Ethernet** — one cable carries **data + power**. **PSE** (Power Sourcing Equipment, e.g., PoE switch) sends power; **PD** (Powered Device, e.g., camera) receives it.

cards.front: The three PoE standards (in order of power)?
What is Ethernet TSN and why needed?
cards.back: **Time-Sensitive Networking** (IEEE **802.1**) = deterministic, real-time Ethernet (low latency, minimal jitter). Needed because plain Ethernet is **best-effort** — no timing guarantee — unacceptable for cyber-physical systems.
**Time sync (802.1AS)**, **traffic scheduling (802.1Qbv)**, **traffic shaping (802.1Qav)**, **frame preemption (802.1Qbu)** — urgent frames jump the queue, **resource reservation (802.1Qcc)**.
Sends **data over existing AC power lines** — overlays high-freq data (kHz–MHz) on 50/60 Hz power, via **OFDM/FSK/PSK**, with filters separating them. Used in **smart grid/meters**.
**Unlicensed** = anyone can use (no licence), e.g., 2.4 GHz **ISM** (WiFi, Zigbee, BLE, LoRa). **Licensed** = auctioned to telecom operators (**cellular**: NB-IoT, LTE-M, 5G).

cards.front: Why does IoT favour unlicensed bands?
cards.back: **Cost-free** (no licence fee), **global** harmonised standards, **scalable** (billions coexist), **innovation-friendly**. Trade-off: **interference** (crowded commons).
**Short** (<10 cm–100 m): NFC/RFID, BLE, Zigbee. **Medium** (100 m–km): WiFi, Z-Wave. **Long/LPWAN** (>5 km–tens of km): LoRa, Sigfox. Range ↔ data-rate ↔ power trade-off.
**IEEE 802.15.4**, **2.4 GHz** ISM, **mesh**, 20–250 kbps, **AES-128**, up to **65,000** devices, coin-cell battery for years. 'The language smart-home devices speak.'
**Coordinator** (1 per net): starts PAN, picks channel/PAN ID, Trust Center/hub. **Router**: stays awake, relays (mesh backbone). **End Device**: battery, sleeps, doesn't relay.
**PHY+MAC (802.15.4)**: radio, CSMA/CA, ACKs. **NWK**: network forming, routing. **APS**: security, binding, groups. **Application (ZCL clusters)**: On/Off, Level, Temperature as attributes/commands.

cards.front: How do Zigbee end devices save power?
cards.back: They **sleep**; their **router parent buffers** downlink frames. On waking, the end device sends a **MAC Data Request** to pull queued data → years on a coin cell.
**BLE** = small packets, short bursts, sleeps → **~100× less power**; for IoT. **Classic** = continuous two-way, always on, longer range + higher throughput (audio/streaming).

**GAP** (Generic Access Profile): discovery, advertising, connections, roles. **GATT** (Generic Attribute Profile): the **data model** — **services** (e.g., Heart Rate) + **characteristics** (values).
**Central** = phone/gateway (initiates, controls). **Peripheral** = sensor/thing (advertises, provides data). Architectural **asymmetry** (e.g., phone ↔ smart band).
**Advertise** (ch 37/38/39) → **discover & connect** → **pair & bond** (AES-128, store keys) → **GATT service discovery** → **data transfer** (Notifications no-ACK / Indications ACK) → **sleep**.

cards.front: WiFi for IoT — standard, bands, key advantage?
cards.back: **IEEE 802.11**; bands **2.4/5/6 GHz**; star topology. Key advantage: **native IP, no gateway translation** needed. Drawback: **high power** (mains devices).
**802.11ah** — sub-GHz (~900 MHz) WiFi variant for **longer range + lower power**, purpose-built for IoT (bridges toward LPWAN while keeping IP).
**LoRa** = the PHY radio modulation (**Chirp Spread Spectrum, CSS**). **LoRaWAN** = the network/MAC protocol on top. Topology: **star-of-stars**.
**End devices** (sensors), **Gateways** (transparent RF→IP relays, redundant), **Network Server** (the brain: dedup, auth, ADR, routing), **Application Server** (decrypts/visualises with AppSKey).

**Class A**: receive only after uplink → **best battery** (default). **Class B**: scheduled (beacon) receive slots → predictable downlink. **Class C**: always-open receiver → **mains-powered**, instant downlink.
**NwkSKey** = integrity (device↔network server). **AppSKey** = confidentiality (device↔app server). Activation: **OTAA** (dynamic, secure) vs **ABP** (static, simpler/less secure). AES-128.
Uses **licensed** (carrier) spectrum. Techs: **GSM-IoT** (2G), **NB-IoT**, **LTE-M**, **5G NR (mMTC)**. Advantage: ubiquitous coverage, no gateways; cost: subscription.
**NB-IoT** = lowest power, deep indoor coverage, **stationary** very-low-rate sensors. **LTE-M** = higher data rate, supports **mobility & voice** (moving/richer devices). Both 3GPP LPWAN.
**Message-oriented (Publish/Subscribe)** — broker, async, decoupled: **MQTT, AMQP**. **Request/Response (Client/Server)**: **HTTP, CoAP**.

cards.front: TCP vs UDP mapping for IoT protocols?
cards.back: **TCP** (reliable): MQTT, HTTP, AMQP. **UDP** (lightweight, no handshake): CoAP, DDS — lower overhead for constrained/lossy links.

**Request/response** = a **phone call** (both present, client asks/server answers). **Pub/sub** = a **noticeboard** (publisher posts to a topic, subscribers read anytime, decoupled) → scales to many intermittent devices.
**Publisher** sends to a **topic** → **Broker** (central server) routes → **Subscribers** of that topic receive. Pub & sub are **decoupled**; event-driven; **2-byte** header.
**0 — at most once** (fire-and-forget). **1 — at least once** (guaranteed but may **duplicate**). **2 — exactly once** (handshake; financial/control data).

cards.front: MQTT retained message vs Last Will (LWT)?
cards.back: **Retained** = broker stores the **last** message on a topic, sent to **new** subscribers immediately. **LWT** = predefined message published if a client **disconnects unexpectedly**.
**Auth**: username/password (CONNECT), tokens/certs. **Encryption**: **TLS/SSL on port 8883**. **Access control**: per-topic **ACLs**. Brokers: Mosquitto, HiveMQ, EMQX, AWS IoT Core.
**Constrained Application Protocol** — 'HTTP for tiny things'. **RESTful** (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) over **UDP**, tiny headers, **DTLS** security, supports **multicast**, discovery, observe.
**CON** = reliable: expects an **ACK**, retransmits if none → reliability over lossy UDP. **NON** = fire-and-forget. **Message IDs** match responses & detect duplicates.
**CoAP**: UDP, DTLS, request/response **+ Observe**, **multicast**. **HTTP**: TCP, TLS, request/response (web). **MQTT**: TCP, TLS, **publish/subscribe** (cloud devices).
**`/.well-known/core`** — devices auto-discover available resources, simplifying dynamic IoT where devices join/leave frequently. Resources are URIs, e.g., `coap://sensor1.local/temp`.

**Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition** — monitor/control industrial processes. Components: **field devices** (sensors/actuators), **RTU/PLC**, **comm network** (Modbus/DNP3), **master + HMI** (operator).

Edge devices run lightweight **CoAP/MQTT**; the **gateway/cloud converts to HTTP/REST** (which all web services/browsers speak) for integration. WebSocket = real-time; AMQP = enterprise pub/sub; DDS = P2P real-time.
